comment: Task T3.2: train the complete models (segmentation + hierarchical CATH classifier) on CATH only. The fixed protocol -- seeds, dataset version, checkpoint metric, early stopping, computing budget -- lives in src/domaino/train/protocol.py, not here, so a run cannot quietly change it.
comment_training: Both architectures use these same settings, which is what T3.2's 'under the same conditions' requires. max_tokens is a padded-residue budget rather than a batch size because chain lengths span 1 to 4128; accumulate_steps buys a larger effective batch without the memory of one.
comment_source_aware: T2.6's source-aware composite loss is off for T3.2 and on for T3.3. T3.2 trains on CATH alone, where every source mask is open, so the only thing source_aware would change is the shape of the residue objective -- it splits the 3-way cross-entropy into separate assignment and boundary terms. Turning it on here would make the T3.2 runs already in reports/experiments/ irreproducible from this file for no experimental gain. T3.3, which adds Pfam and TED, cannot run without it: those sources are silent about unannotated residues, and the T2.3 loss would read that silence as linker.
comment_accumulation: accumulate_steps is 1: at max_tokens 24000 a batch already holds ~86 chains, so accumulating gave an effective batch of ~344 and only ~570 optimiser steps per epoch. Memory is not the constraint at 40 GB, so the steps are worth more than the larger batch. Both architectures use the same value, as T3.2 requires.
